answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each identity expensive to keep, not to create: every account posts a refundable stake, and a rotating committee of peers runs surprise audits against hidden test cases. Failure burns the stake and permanently ties the account's hash to the fraud, so a farmer juggling fifty fake identities pays for all of them at once. Trust becomes a ridge built from repeated audited work, not a relic any newcomer can forge cheaply, like timber graded by inspectors rather than self-declared.
